quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO, non-GAAP): revenue $231.3 million, up 34.2% year-over-year, driven by ECP and advanced packaging; total shipments $240.7 million, up 53.6%; gross margin 46.5% versus 48.2%, above the midpoint of the 42%-48% long-term target and a recovery from the low 40% range in Q3 and Q4 of 2025 on favorable mix and a lower inventory-provision impact; operating margin 18.1% versus 20.7%; net income per diluted share $0.34 versus $0.46; net cash $924.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $231.3 million (+34.2%); shipments $240.7 million (+53.6%); gross margin 46.5%; operating margin 18.1%; EPS $0.34

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 product mix: single wafer cleaning, Ultra C Tahoe and semi-critical cleaning $122.5 million, down 5.5% (about 53% of sales) with very little contribution from new products; ECP (front-end and packaging), furnace and other technologies $84.2 million, up 204.9% (36.4% of sales), mostly ECP front-end with very little from furnace; advanced packaging excluding ECP, services and spares $24.5 million, up 62% (10.6% of sales). For full-year 2026 management expects the cleaning mix to normalize towards the 65% level, similar to 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: cleaning $122.5 million (-5.5%); ECP/furnace $84.2 million (+204.9%); advanced packaging $24.5 million (+62%); cleaning mix towards the 65% level for 2026

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook reiterated: revenue $1.08 billion-$1.175 billion (introduced mid-January), implying 25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint; annual shipment growth expected to outpace revenue growth. CFO now expects about $175 million of 2026 capital expenditures (Q1 capex $22 million); 2026 opex plan R&D 16%-18%, sales and marketing 8%-9%, G&A 5%-6% of sales; effective tax rate 8%-10%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $1.08 billion-$1.175 billion (25% growth at midpoint); capex about $175 million

quarterly_data.signal: Demand color: cleaning shipments grew 32% in Q1 despite the revenue decline, which the CEO attributed to new-application problems in 2025 that have now mostly been solved with customers (helped by Lingang production); about 15% of Q1 shipments were catch-up of tools rescheduled from Q4 2025. The CEO said PO receipts in the first six months were 'almost like a 50% increase' versus the prior-year first six months.
quarterly_data.figure: cleaning shipments +32%; about 15% of Q1 shipments catch-up from Q4; PO receipts almost like a 50% increase (first six months)

quarterly_data.signal: Single-wafer SPM ramp: management expects significant production ramping of the single-wafer hot SPM product line, with 15-20 units to be delivered by year-end to customers in Asia or China (first deliveries in Q1); SPM shipments ramp through the year with revenue in later quarters. The CEO said SPM cleaning occupies 30% of the cleaning market and expects ACM's maintenance-free nozzle design to take significant share from the market leader; fine particle removal is critical for advanced-node GAA logic and memory such as HBM. Validation on the Lingang mini-line led to volume orders from numerous customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 15-20 SPM tools to be delivered by year-end; SPM 30% of the cleaning market

quarterly_data.signal: Electroplating (ECP) revenue growth was driven by front-end plating, HBM and 2.5D advanced packaging, which also drive ACM's advanced-packaging wet tools (coater, developer, wet etcher, PR stripper, cleaning). ACM delivered the world's first 515 by 510 millimeter panel-level horizontal plating tool in Q4 2025 and is building a backlog for both 515 by 510 millimeter and 310 by 310 millimeter panels; it expects successful evaluation to lead to a volume production order for 515 by 510 and additional 310 by 310 evaluation later in 2026, with panel horizontal copper plating entering revenue and shipments in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: panel sizes 515 by 510 millimeter and 310 by 310 millimeter

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced-packaging shipments in Q1: a panel-level vacuum cleaning system to a leading global semiconductor packaging manufacturer outside mainland China, and multiple wafer-level advanced packaging systems to a leading OSAT customer in Singapore (transcribed as 'leading offset customer in Singapore'); customers not named. Management positions its wet-process and plating portfolio for 2.5D/3D integration including TSV-based architectures.

New-product pipeline: the high-throughput 300 WPH KrF track tool (first evaluation tool delivered last September) is progressing toward mass-production qualification in 2026, with interest in standalone and scanner-integrated configurations; vertical furnace tools (LPCVD, oxidation, thermal ALD, anneal) are under evaluation at multiple customers with more meaningful revenue expected later in 2026; ACM announced the ACM Planetary Family (eight product families) at SEMICON China. Validating customer wafers on the Lingang mini-line should cut on-site qualification to the order of a few quarters rather than more than a year.
quarterly_data.figure: 300 WPH KrF track tool; eight product family

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and footprint: raw-material inventory rose to $377.9 million (up $28.3 million quarter-over-quarter) on strategic purchases to support production plans and mitigate potential supply chain risk; total inventory $738 million, with finished goods mainly first tools under customer evaluation. Oregon remains on track for an in-house demo lab and the capability to produce U.S.-made tools by year end of 2026; the February ACM Shanghai minority share sale raised about $110 million of gross proceeds for U.S. and global expansion, and in April ACM Shanghai announced a proposed H-share secondary listing in Hong Kong.
quarterly_data.figure: raw materials $377.9 million (up $28.3 million QoQ); total inventory $738 million; $110 million gross proceeds
